evidence.assertion: Complete ownership, preserved original contracts, explicit local interaction routes and rejection of missing, duplicate, misowned, downgraded or silently changed requirements.

tests.name: every semantic, interaction and later deliverable has exactly one stable owner
missing and duplicate owners fail even in an unaccepted batch
moving an obligation to the wrong batch cannot satisfy ownership
empty semantic batches and missing late gates cannot disappear
only the named B16 families can be deferred
missing interaction families and explicit alternative routes fail
interaction evidence cannot be downgraded to provider or command
negative interaction routes and independent expectations are mandatory
changed interaction text requires reviewed contract and route migration
changed applicability and N/A reasons require explicit migration
new requirements must be explicitly assigned before they enter scope
splits name exact old/new contracts and preserved behavior

evidence.assertion: Selected and previously accepted requirements need current exact evidence; executed failures, missing editor proof, stale contracts and unsupported scopes cannot pass.

tests.name: scoped acceptance permits pending future batches but requires selected proof
accepted batches must pass again with current evidence
any executed failure blocks acceptance even outside selected scope
missing editor results and deferred batch selection cannot pass
stale contracts and N/A cannot substitute for current gate or interaction proof
TAP evidence distinguishes success, failure, ignored and duplicate tests
gate evidence requires exact executed tests and cannot use candidate names
gate evidence rejects wrong layers, duplicate mappings and unknown obligations
stale contracts and N/A cannot substitute for current gate or interaction proof
final acceptance cannot silently drop unresolved baseline issues

evidence.assertion: Checkpoint validation enforces batch prerequisites, exact remaining scope, current acceptance contracts, reopening, local profile and source provenance.

tests.name: checkpoint acceptance advances exact remaining scope and retains provenance
forged order, duplicate acceptance and stale remaining IDs fail
new, removed or changed accepted scope requires explicit reopening
reopening records the prior acceptance and keeps later regression gates
checkpoint rejects missing source identity, failed commands and changed profiles
checkpoint rejects wrong active child and machine-specific artifact paths
source identity includes edits, new files and deletions but excludes its own checkpoint
local gates pin the execution profile while ordinary existing CI stays portable
later audits preserve earlier failure reports and logs
